la:verb:obeo.gloss: to go towards, go to meet; to oppose, face
senses: to go towards, go to meet; to oppose, face
to arrive at, reach, come to
to undertake a task, take charge of, take part in
to traverse, travel over, travel through
to fall, perish, pass away, die (mortem or diem obeo)
la:verb:obeo.html:
ŏb-ĕo, īvi or ĭi (obivi, ; ; ;
contr. obit for obiit,; ; ), ĭtum, 4 (lengthened form, obinunt obeunt, Paul. ex Müll.), v. n. and a.
Neutr., to go or come to or towards, to come in, to go to meet, go against (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
In gen.: donec vis obiit,until force intervene,: dum acris vis obeat,: obit infera Perseus in loca, (Grot. 718): ad omnes hostium conatus,to go to meet, to oppose,. —
In partic.
Of constellations, to go down, to set: abditur Orion, obit et Lepus abditus umbrā, (Grot. 716); : an sidera obirent, nascerenturve,.—Of the sun: in reliquis orientis aut obeuntis solis partibus,: in undis Sol fit uti videatur obire et condere lumen,.—Hence, to pass by: tres noctes,.—
Pregn., to fall, perish (syn.: occido, pereo, occumbo). —Of cities: et Agamede obiit et Hiera,; .— —Hence, to die: malo cruciatu ut pereas atque obeas cito,; ; tecum vivere amem, tecum obeam libens,: simul se cum illis obituros,: gaudio,to die of joy,: morbo,of a disease,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; : voluntariā morte obiit,; ; : morte subitā,: repentinā morte,; .—
Act. (freq. and class.), to go or come to a thing or place.
In gen.: Acherontem nunc obibo, Enn. ap. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. ob, p. 201 Müll. (Trag. v. 278 Vahl.): tantum restitisset urbis, quantum flamma obire non potuisset,to reach,.—
In partic.
To travel over or through; to wander through, traverse, visit: nec vero Alcides tantum telluris obivit,: tantas regiones barbarorum pedibus obiit,: villas,to visit,: comitia,: cenas,. —
To run over with the eyes, to survey, review: oculis exercitum,to survey,: omnia visu,.—In speaking, to go over, mention, recount: oratione omnes civitates,to enumerate,.—
To go around, surround, overspread, envelop (poet.): chlamydem limbus obibat Aureus,: clipeum,.—
To apply

one's self to, to engage in, attend to any business or undertaking; to enter upon an office; to discharge, perform, execute, accomplish any thing: obeundi negotii studio tot loca adire,: hereditatum obeundarum causā,to enter upon, take possession of,: facinus,: pugnas,to engage in battle,; : judicia,: legationem,to enter upon, undertake,; : consularia munera,: munus vigiliarum,: publica ac privata officia,: neque privatam rem ... neque publicam,: ne ad omnia simul obire unus non possit,: rusticum opus,: bella,: sacra,: imperia,to perform, execute,.—

To meet: vadimonium,to meet one's bail, appear at the appointed time,: diem,to appear on the day appointed,; ; : annum petitiones tuae,i. e. to be a candidate the first year the law permits,.—Hence, diem suum obire, to die: ea diem suom obiit,; Sulp. ap. ; ; so, diem supremum,; and simply, diem,: mortem,; ; hence, in the pass.: morte obitā (sc. ob rem publicam),.—Hence, P. a. (anteand post-class.): ŏbĭtus, a, um, for mortuus, dead, Liv. Andron. ap. P.: obiti, the dead: obitis libatione profunditur,: OBITAE,.

la:noun:obex.gloss: a bolt, bar; a barrier, wall
senses: a bolt, bar; a barrier, wall
la:noun:obex.html:
ōbex, obĭcis (objĭcis), m. and f. (of either gender indifferently; very rare in
nom. sing.; acc. not found, v. Neue, Formenl. 1, p. 489) [obicio, that which is cast or placed before; hence], a bolt, bar; a barrier, wall (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. or Cæs.).
Lit.: obices pessuli, serae, Paul. ex Müll.: fultosque emuniit obice postes,; cf. : ferrati portarum obices,: obices portarum subversi,; : diffractis portarum obicibus,: infirmā scamellorum obice fultae fores, App. ap. P.: saxi,: ecce maris magnā claudit nos obice pontus,: quā vi maria alta tumescant Obicibus ruptis, their barriers, i. e. their rocky shores, ; —
Transf., a hinderance, impediment, obstacle: apud hanc obicem,: per obices viarum,; ; : nullae obices, nulli contumeliarum gradus, obstacles to admission, ; .

la:verb:obedo.gloss: to eat, eat away, or devour
senses: to eat, eat away, or devour
to waste away or become lean
la:verb:obedo.html:
ŏb-ĕdo, ēdi, ēsum, ĕre,
to eat, eat away, devour (used only in the part. perf. and P. a.).—Trop.: nec obesa cavamine terra est,.—Hence, P. a.: ŏbēsus, a, um.
Wasted away, lean, meagre: corpore pectoreque undique obeso, Laev. ap. ; and ap. : (obesum hic notavimus proprie magis quam usitate dictum pro exili atque gracilento, Gell. ib.: obesum gracile et exile, Non. l. l.).—
Mid., that has eaten itself fat; hence, in gen., fat, stout, plump: obesus pinguis quasi ob edendum factus, Paul. ex Müll. (not in Cic.; perh. not ante-Aug.; syn.: opimus, pinguis): corpus neque gracile, neque obesum,; cf. : turdus,: sus,: terga,: cervix,.—Sup.: obesissimus venter,; ; .—Poet.: fauces obesae,swollen,.—
Trop., gross, coarse, heavy, dull (poet.): munera quid mihi quidve tabellas Mittis nec firmo juveni neque naris obesae? that has not a quick nose, that is not nice or delicate, = obtusae, ; so, aures,: mens,: obeso somno mori, idle, lazy, inactive, of bees, .

la:verb:obedio.gloss: to obey, yield obedience to (+dative of person obeyed)
